## What was added
`tests/draw.test.ts` already had three direct-state tests proving shapes survive clicks with `eraseOnClick: false` (empty square, opponent piece, own piece, via `drag.start` with a stubbed `dom`). The gap those tests leave is the public path: config merge and real event wiring. So I added one end-to-end test in the same file:

**`drawings survive a click on the full board when eraseOnClick is false`**
- Builds a real board via `Chessground(wrap, { trustAllEvents: true, drawable: { enabled: true, eraseOnMovablePieceClick: true, eraseOnClick: false } })` — proving the option flows through `Config` → `deepMerge` into state.
- Stubs `getBoundingClientRect` (jsdom reports zero-size rects) and clears the memoized bounds so `getKeyAtDomPos` maps coordinates to squares.
- `api.setShapes([{ orig: 'e2', dest: 'e4', brush: 'red' }])`, then dispatches real `mousedown` `MouseEvent`s at the centers of `a1` (empty), `e2` (own piece), and `a8` (opponent piece) — unselecting between clicks so each has no `previouslySelected` guard.
- Asserts the shape survives all three clicks.
